title: Your photo, your bio and profiles that tell one story

say: Your photo, your bio, and profiles that tell one story.
This is the video for module two of Personal Branding and Online Presence.
Your photo and bio are the two things almost everyone sees. On WhatsApp, your photo sits beside every message you send, so it must show your face clearly.

panel.heading: A professional photo with your phone
items: Face a window, or stand in open shade
Plain wall or a tidy workspace behind you
Camera at eye level: head and shoulders
Natural smile. Take 20 or more shots
Crop to a square. No heavy beauty filters

say: Light first. Face a window, or go outside in the shade in the morning or late afternoon. Never stand with the window behind you, because your face turns dark.

say: Choose a plain wall or a neat workspace. Remove clutter, laundry and bright patterns.

panel.heading: A professional photo with your phone

say: Hold the camera at eye level, about an arm's length away, or ask someone to help. Show your head and the top of your shoulders.

say: Wear what a client would expect to see you in at work. Smile naturally, look at the lens, and take 20 or more shots.

say: Crop to a square and brighten a little if needed. Avoid heavy filters, because clients should recognise you when they meet you.
Then use that same photo on WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn.

say: A bio is your positioning statement, shaped for one platform. Start from the short, medium and long versions you wrote in module one.

panel.heading: Every bio does four jobs

Who it is for
One proof point
What to do next

say: Every good bio says what you do, and who it is for.

say: It gives one proof point.

say: And it tells the reader what to do next: how to contact you or order.

say: For example, Chiamaka makes adire and ankara bags in Abeokuta. Her old bio said: Daughter of Zion. Bags. DM for price. It says nothing about style, delivery or quality.

panel.heading: Chiamaka rewrites her Instagram bio
right: Delivery across Nigeria in 3 to 5 days

say: Her new bio: Handmade adire and ankara bags for work and owambe. Made in Abeokuta. Delivery across Nigeria in 3 to 5 days. Order on WhatsApp below.
It is about 130 characters, inside Instagram's limit of 150. Her faith can still show in her posts, but it no longer replaces what buyers need to know.

panel.heading: Chiamaka rewrites her Instagram bio
right: Delivery across Nigeria in 3 to 5 days

say: LinkedIn is where recruiters, employers and many business buyers check people. Fill it from the top down, starting with your photo and a simple banner.

panel.heading: Fill the top of your profile first
items: Photo and banner
Headline: skill, who you help, a result
About: who you help, proof, how to reach you
Experience: action verbs and true numbers
Skills, Featured and Recommendations

say: Your headline is not just your job title. For example, Kemi changed Customer Service Officer at a bank into Customer Experience Specialist, resolving complaints and improving service in banking.

panel.heading: Fill the top of your profile first
items: Photo and banner
Headline: skill, who you help, a result
About: who you help, proof, how to reach you
Experience: action verbs and true numbers
Skills, Featured and Recommendations

say: In About, put your strongest sentence first, because only the first two or three lines show before see more.

say: In Experience, start lines with action verbs and show results, not duties. Kemi wrote: trained 8 new staff on complaint handling.

say: For many women in Nigeria, WhatsApp is the shop counter, and Instagram and Facebook are the shop window. WhatsApp Business is free. Add a catalogue, so customers can browse your prices without asking how much each time.

cards.d: Products with photos, prices and descriptions, so customers browse without asking how much.
Automatic replies: welcome new customers, and say when you will be back.
Saved answers for prices and delivery. Labels like New order, Paid, Delivered.

say: Set a greeting message that thanks the person, points to the catalogue and says how fast you reply. Set an away message that says when you will be back.

cards.d: Products with photos, prices and descriptions, so customers browse without asking how much.
Automatic replies: welcome new customers, and say when you will be back.
Saved answers for prices and delivery. Labels like New order, Paid, Delivered.

say: Save quick replies for prices, account details and delivery terms. And use labels, so no paid order is forgotten in a busy week.

Automatic replies: welcome new customers, and say when you will be back.
Saved answers for prices and delivery. Labels like New order, Paid, Delivered.

say: For example, Aisha sells modest fashion in Kaduna. She listed every field on every platform and found three different names, and an old phone line on Facebook.
She chose Aisha Modest Wear everywhere, with the same photo, the same positioning line and her current WhatsApp link. Now a customer moving between her apps never wonders if it is the same person.

Keep your account details in a quick reply, so you never mistype them. Confirm every payment in your own bank or wallet app before you send goods, because screenshots of transfers can be faked. And test your WhatsApp click-to-chat link before you publish it.

panel.heading: Before you send any goods
items: Account details saved in a quick reply
Payment confirmed in your own bank app
Never trust a transfer screenshot alone
Click-to-chat link tested before you publish

say: Now your practice. Take at least 20 photos and pick the best one. Write your WhatsApp About line and Instagram bio using the four jobs.
Rebuild your LinkedIn headline and About. Fix every mismatch across your platforms, and add at least 5 items to your catalogue.
Screenshot each change for your after album. Now continue with the lessons below.
